amm_to_clob.description: Buy base on the AMM pool and sell it into the order book's bids

executable_base.description: Base quantity tradable before the pool's marginal price reaches the book level prices; "0" when not open

gap_bps.description: Gap between the book's best price and the pool price after the AMM fee in basis points, rounded half-up to 2 decimals; positive means open; null when the direction cannot be evaluated

net_quote_profit.description: Quote profit of executable_base after the taker transfer fees; "0" when not open; null when a transfer rate is unknown

status.description: open when gap_bps is positive; no_opportunity otherwise, or when the direction cannot be evaluated (no usable pool or the book side empty); a defined computation and not advice

clob_to_amm.description: Buy base from the order book's asks and sell it into the AMM pool

executable_base.description: Base quantity tradable before the pool's marginal price reaches the book level prices; "0" when not open

gap_bps.description: Gap between the book's best price and the pool price after the AMM fee in basis points, rounded half-up to 2 decimals; positive means open; null when the direction cannot be evaluated

net_quote_profit.description: Quote profit of executable_base after the taker transfer fees; "0" when not open; null when a transfer rate is unknown

status.description: open when gap_bps is positive; no_opportunity otherwise, or when the direction cannot be evaluated (no usable pool or the book side empty); a defined computation and not advice

triangles.description: Present only with include_triangles=true: the cycles of the USD registry coins (RLUSD, USDC) via XRP, both directions, from top of book

gap_bps.description: Product of the top-of-book leg rates after the taker transfer fees, as basis points above 1, rounded half-up to 2 decimals; null when a leg's book side is empty or a transfer rate is unknown

path.description: The cycle as symbols, from XRP back to XRP, for example ["XRP","RLUSD","USDC","XRP"]

top_size_xrp.description: Smallest top-of-book size of the legs, each carried back to XRP through the preceding legs' rates; null when gap_bps is null

description: Whether a pair's AMM pool and its order book are apart after the AMM fee: per direction the gap, the executable size and the profit after transfer fees. When to use: To find whether a pair's AMM pool and its funded order book are apart after the AMM fee, in which direction, how much base the gap allows and the profit after transfer fees, optionally with the cycles of the USD registry stablecoins via XRP. Prefer another tool: To estimate the cost of a trade of a given size, CLOB against AMM (use `/v1/xrpl/slippage`), or to read the order book levels (use `/v1/xrpl/orderbook`) or an AMM pool (use `/v1/xrpl/amm/{a}/{b}`); the answer measures the ledger and is not an executable quote. Example: xrpl_metrics_arbitrage {"base":"XRP","quote":"524C555344000000000000000000000000000000.rMxCKbEDwqr76QuheSUMdEGf4B9xJ8m5De"} Paid: 0.01452 USDC or 0.0121 EURC per call on Solana mainnet, VAT included.

base.description: Base currency of the pair: `XRP`, or `CODE.issuer`: `CODE` is a 3-character standard code or 40 hexadecimal digits, and `issuer` is a classic XRPL address. Standard codes are case-sensitive: `usd` and `USD` are different tokens, so send the exact code. A standard code uses letters, digits or `?!@#$%^&*<>(){}[]|` and is never `XRP`; percent-encode the symbols in a URL (for example `%3F` for `?`). A 40-hex code is read in any case, and the 40-hex form of a standard code means that code.

include_triangles.description: The string "true" adds the cycles of the USD registry coins (RLUSD, USDC) via XRP; "false" or omitted leaves them out

quote.description: Quote currency of the pair, different from base: `XRP`, or `CODE.issuer`: `CODE` is a 3-character standard code or 40 hexadecimal digits, and `issuer` is a classic XRPL address. Standard codes are case-sensitive: `usd` and `USD` are different tokens, so send the exact code. A standard code uses letters, digits or `?!@#$%^&*<>(){}[]|` and is never `XRP`; percent-encode the symbols in a URL (for example `%3F` for `?`). A 40-hex code is read in any case, and the 40-hex form of a standard code means that code.
